title.narrative: Supporting Safe Recovery of Travel and Tourism

description.narrative: The goal of the proposal is to increase Cook Islands economic resilience through a safe recovery of travel and tourism in Cook Islands and the key objective is to strengthen the capacity and readiness of Cook Islands to safely open its borders to support a safe travel zone with New Zealand.

description.narrative: Cook Islands readiness for safe recovery of travel and tourism improved.

100% recovery of tourist arrivals to pre-pandemic level, 171, 550 in FY2019) Achievement: 113,348 Progress/Status: Visitor arrivals have shown improvement from FY2021=26,330 to FY2022=113,348 and FY2023=127,529. Data Source: a. Government Budgets and Financial Reports/Statements b. Cook Islands Migration Statistics, MFEM Actual value: 113,348
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Airport and border readiness improved. Indicator: Civil works to extend 258.47m2 to the existing airport structure (including gender responsive design features) completed by 2027. (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: 1. RFQ for Airport civil works released 12 Oct 2022 and due 25 Oct 2022 (Fiji time), with only one responsive bidder. 2. The BER noted that the bid received exceed the budget for this procurement package due to costs escalation in raw materials impacting the construction industry. Government through the BER and an official letter received in December 2022 requested ADB support for additional financing. Due to uncertainty in funding, a decision was reached to defer the rebidding upon securing additional financing. 3. ADB Project team secured (in-principle) $2 million from ADF Thematic Pool on 27 June 2023 and this was relayed to government through MFEM - addressing action item 1 of the November 2022 MOU. 4. Mid-term review in June 2023 facilitated a discussion between ADB, MFEM, PMU and Airport Authority Cook Islands to revisit the design of the extension to ensure it aligns with the Masterplan for the Rarotonga Airport terminal. The general scope remains apart from minor modifications to ensure it is fit for purpose. 5. Revised design and costings yet to be finalized. During meeting between a meeting between ADB and government, MFEM advised that an updated design and costs estimates should be ready by end of 2023 or latest February 2024. 6. Revisions to the design and the procurement method to include updated costings and scope to be discussed with stakeholders then relisted by Q4 2024. ADB to keep monitoring! 7. Pending additional funding and approval through ADB Thematic Pipeline prior to re-listing the project. Funding is scheduled for approval on 11 Dec 2024. Non-structural changes only are to be implemented to the AACI design. 8. JFPR02 package issued 9 Sep 2024 and bids closed 4 Nov 2024. BER drafted and shared with ADB in Dec 2024 - ongoing review. 9. Additional funding approved 11 Dec 2024 and awaiting legal opinion for declaration of effectiveness. 10. Additional financing became effective in Dec 2024. 11. Package JFPR02 was awarded in March 2025. 12. Works commenced from 19 May 2025 and progressing well with a few variations using the contingency provision of the contract. 13. Works scheduled for completion by 30 January 2026. Data Source: Project Team quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Airport and border readiness improved. Indicator: Results of the reconfiguration civil works, providing an example for other Pacific DMCs and Civil Aviation Authorities to learn and replicate, published by 2027. Progress/Status: 1. Works has not commenced and therefore, the briefing note was not published as planned. 2. A mid-term review was conducted in June 2023, where the target was revised to Q4 2024. The target is to be further assessed during project implementation as it may need to be updated to Q3/Q4 2025 upon securing an extension to the project life of this project. 3. Knowledge product - Gender study on the aviation sector was completed in May and shared with stakeholders. Data Source: Briefing Note published Actual value:

Data Source: Quarterly Project Reports Actual value:

Output: Health readiness improved. Indicator: Civil works for minor upgrades to the primary healthcare facility (including considerations for maternal health and GBV services) completed by 2024. Progress/Status: 1. RFQ for civil works to be finalized by end of October 2022 for submission to ADB for clearance. 2. Contract awarded in March 2023 and works commenced April 2023. 3. ADB no objections for two contract variations: i) furniture and ii) ICT fit out, have been approved. 4. Building works were completed in September 2023. The completion of the furniture and ICT fit out was expected in December 2023 however there were delays with shipment. Completion expected end of Q1 2024. 5. Project completed 25 March 2024. Furniture fit out and ICT installation has been completed by contractor. Final walk through and issuing of practical completion carried out in September 2024. 6. Completion report to be finalized and shared with ADB. 7. Defects liability ends 10 May 2025. 8. Facility now utilized by Te Marae Ora (Ministry of Health) and is functional. Data Source: Project Team quarterly report and Briefing Note published. Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Health readiness improved. Indicator: Medical waste treatment system procured and installed by 2024. Progress/Status: 1. RFQ for medical equipment closed on 13 September 2022 and bid evaluation report due to ADB by end of October 2022. Contract award expected mid of November 2022. 2. RFQ was relisted in December however due to non-conformance, the package is to undergo revision of technical specifications and relisted. 3. RFQ was relisted in April 2023 and BER submitted August 2023. 4. ADB's no objection to CA approved on 7 September 2023. Discussions are ongoing between PMU and supplier. Contract was signed in December 2023 and the product order has been placed with the supplier. 5. Medical unit has been fabricated and en route to NZ March 2024, impacted installation date by several months. 6. Ongoing work regarding removal of containers and cladding to protect system is almost complete (90%). 7. Medical unit installed and in operation end of August 2024. 8. Completion report to be finalized and shared with ADB. 9. Defects liability ends 1 October 2025. Data Source: Project Team quarterly report and Briefing Note published.
